points.t: Facial papules and pustules in a baby. Comedones point to true acne; pustules without comedones suggest cephalic pustulosis.
Sebaceous glands driven by maternal and neonatal androgens, plus Cutibacterium.
Neonatal: observe and cleanse gently. Infantile: BPO ± topical retinoid. No tetracyclines under 12.
Acne between ages 1 and 6, signs of hyperandrogenism, or nodular or scarring disease. Refer.

points: **Neonatal:** comedones on the scalp, chest and back; inflammatory lesions on the cheeks, chin and forehead.
**Infantile:** mainly the cheeks; can be more inflammatory or nodular.

cards.name: Neonatal cephalic pustulosis
cards.clue: No or few comedones; sometimes responds to topical antifungal

cards.name: Periorificial dermatitis
cards.clue: Around the mouth and eyes; often steroid-related

items.t: Suspected hyperandrogenism (accelerated growth, body odour, pubic hair, clitoromegaly).
Nodular or scarring disease, or treatment failure.

pearls.t: Reassure parents that neonatal acne is not caused by poor hygiene.
Do not use adult OTC acne kits on infants without checking age licences.
Persistent facial pustules in a neonate: consider cephalic pustulosis rather than true acne.
